commits.author: mcwitt-agent
commits.message:
[gpu] Pin the validated ragged all-to-all PJRT wheel (#9179)

Pin the ARM64 CUDA 13 PJRT wheel to XLA `708c3a4ec79c`, which uses 32
thread blocks of 512 threads, sender-relative peer ordering, and
eight-load copy batches for the opt-in ragged all-to-all device kernel.
The stock JAX, jaxlib, and CUDA plugin generation remains 0.11.1.

[Three matched EP64/GB200 pairs](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/407)
measured 2.766% higher training throughput for the 32 × 256 geometry,
peer ordering, and copy changes versus the previous 152 × 128 kernel. A
separate three-pair comparison measured 0.699% higher throughput for 512
versus 256 threads at fixed 32 blocks, peer ordering, and copy batches.
Each comparison includes all 60 scored steps per run after 20 fixed
warmup steps, including latency spikes; these estimates come from
different run windows and should not be added. They do not establish
reduced spike frequency or long-run convergence.

The [promoted
wheel](https://github.com/marin-community/xla/releases/tag/marin-xla-pjrt-20260915-708c3a4ec79c)
was built on Iris and passed two-device GB200 output correctness and
device-kernel engagement checks. Its immutable release includes the
source revisions, wheel hash, and validation record. The safe CPU suite
passed 1,858 tests; all 11 Tasktrove failures reproduced on unchanged
`main`.


The hero trigger now names the relaunch that deploys this wheel together
with the PDL-off QuACK launchers from #9183: run id
`hero-nopdl-step108k`, initialized from `hero-mix-996f4891-step108k`'s
hourly checkpoint `step-108778`, whose metadata is marked non-temporary
so the old run's later saves keep it. The old run trains 200 steps past
that checkpoint as the paired control for the trial window (#8870).

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Launch the QuACK grouped GEMMs without PDL (#9183)

The three QuACK grouped-GEMM launchers in `quack_moe_cute` now pass
`use_pdl=False`, so the gated, plain, and weight-gradient kernels start
after the preceding kernel completes instead of overlapping it under
programmatic dependent launch.

QuACK 0.6.4's SM100 GEMM executes `griddepcontrol.wait` only in its
TMA-load and CLC-scheduler warps. The MMA and epilogue warps decode
their work tiles from `cu_seqlens` in global memory before any wait, so
a PDL-launched GEMM can read the expert group boundaries before the
previous kernel's writes are visible. Both GPU dumps of the ragged EP
hero hang (#8870, steps 107501 and 108711) show that split: in every
stuck CTA the MMA and epilogue warps retired on a tile the load and
scheduler warps still held as valid, and one cluster retired on its
first tile. The load warp then blocks on the A/B pipeline and the rank
never reaches the next ragged all-to-all barrier.

Cost was measured on the six-GEMM expert MLP forward and backward at the
hero shape (601,088 rows, 6 experts, hidden 6144, intermediate 3072) on
two GB200 nodes, 1,000 iterations per arm, each arm twice per GPU:
median 87.6 ms per iteration with PDL off against 87.7 ms with PDL on on
one node, 88.7 ms against 88.5 ms on the other, within 0.3% and inside
the per-GPU spread. 32,000 iterations ran without a hang or non-finite
value.

The change is a mitigation. Neither probe reproduced the hang in 100,000
launches, and the hero rate is about one hang per 1e6 GPU-steps, so the
change is judged by the recurrence interval on the next hero relaunch.
The probes and their per-arm results are recorded on the issue. The
upstream fix is a `griddepcontrol.wait` in QuACK's MMA and epilogue
warps, which one probe arm exercised with a patched copy of QuACK.

Part of #8870

commits.author: timodonnell
commits.message:
[vibe_check] Add biocorpus prompts and an optional expected continuation (#9178)

biocorpus is in the hero data mix
([`datakit/download/biocorpus.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/biocorpus.py),
pinned to the `2026-07-30` bucket snapshot). These ten prompts ask
whether a checkpoint shows it.

They come in **five in-corpus / held-out pairs**. Reading one completion
tells you little; comparing a pair separates *reproduced this document*
from *knows what this kind of document looks like*.

| pair | in-corpus | held out | why it is held out |
|---|---|---|---|
| myoglobin | `A0A3B3H9I9` medaka | `A0AB13A8W5` zebrafish | TrEMBL
non-representative |
| GreA | `A6LMS3` *Thermosipho* | `P0DYD7` *Thermus aquaticus* | created
2026-09-02 |
| dogma splice | HES4 human | chicken *NDUFB2* | dogma build is
human-only |
| dogma translate | HES4 human | chicken *NDUFB2* | dogma build is
human-only |
| design direction | `A6LMS3` | `P0DYD7` | created 2026-09-02 |

### Exclusion mechanisms, each verified against the built corpus

- biocorpus keeps only **UniRef50 cluster representatives** from TrEMBL,
so an annotated non-representative is excluded by cluster bookkeeping
alone — nothing to do with content
- the dogma build runs on **human genome files only** (`run_v2.sh`), so
any other vertebrate is excluded while staying byte-identical in format
- entries **created after the snapshot** cannot be in it

The third needs per-accession verification, not just a date filter. One
candidate created 2026-09-02 turned out to be in the corpus **four
times**: the accession existed in TrEMBL before the snapshot and was
only later promoted to Swiss-Prot, so `date_created` records promotion
rather than first existence. Every held-out item here was confirmed
absent by accession *and* by full sequence; every in-corpus item
confirmed present. The hit counts corroborate the recipe independently —
the TrEMBL representative appears once, the Swiss-Prot entry twice,
matching `--ordering both` on Swiss-Prot only.

### Design notes

Both proteins are **single-copy genes**. A large paralog family
(olfactory receptors, say) would let a model reproduce most of an
annotation from family knowledge alone. Within each pair the shared
boilerplate is near-identical and the discriminating detail is
entry-specific — the GO process terms differ completely between the two
myoglobins, and the two GreAs differ on "releases sequences of 2 to 3"
vs "7 to 8 nucleotides". The in-corpus organisms are deliberately
obscure, so a correct completion is not explained by general web text.

Every document was rendered by the corpus builder itself, and `prompt +
expected` reconstructs a real training document byte-for-byte. The two
dogma prompts nest: the translate prompt is exactly the splice prompt
plus its expected continuation, so one tests splicing and the other
translation without overlap.

Budgets: worst prompt 1226 tokens, worst expected 548 — inside
`context_length=4096` and `max_new_tokens=1024`.

### `expected`

Optional, unset on the existing 35 prompts. Sampling ignores it (no
reference in `sample.py` or `generation.py`); the report shows it in a
collapsed `<details>` beside the completion, because a factual prompt
cannot be marked by a reader who does not already know the answer.

### For reviewers

`sample_id` digests the spec, which contains the prompt list — so **this
invalidates every cached sample set and re-samples all retained
checkpoints**. The schema change rides along in the same commit for that
reason, since it perturbs the digest too.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: marin-ops-agent[bot]
commits.message:
Delete dead data-path code and fix external-sort spill cleanup (#9170)

`_merge_sorted_frames` wrapped its entire spill-cleanup loop in one
try/except,
so the first `StoragePath.rm()` that raised aborted the loop and
stranded every
remaining run file. Each run holds a full `fan_in` group of the shard's
payload,
and on the inline-runner path the external sort directory lives under
the
stage's object-storage prefix, so one transient delete error left
billable cloud
storage behind. Each run is now deleted independently.

`HtmlToMarkdownConfig` declared fifteen markdownify options
(`autolinks`,
`bullets`, `escape_asterisks`, `wrap_width`, and the rest) as
unannotated class
attributes. They are not dataclass fields, so `markdownify_kwargs` —
which
iterates `fields(self)` — never emitted them, and the converter has
always used
markdownify's own defaults for those options. The values were verbatim
copies of
`MarkdownConverter.DefaultOptions` and were free to drift from it while
reading
as live configuration. `ResiliparseConfig.markdownify_kwargs` goes with
them: it
looked up `markdownify_config`'s fields on `self` and so raised
`AttributeError`
for any caller, of which there were none. Rendering is unchanged.

`K8sResource.api_base`, `collection_path`, and `item_path` built REST
URL paths
for the raw-HTTP Kubernetes client that #4532 replaced with the dynamic
client;
the dynamic client derives its own paths from the enum's `api_group`,
`api_version`, `is_namespaced`, and `plural` metadata, which stays.
`TaskAttempt.with_attempt` and `without_attempt` have had no caller
since #3496
added them. `ShardedDataSource.map_batches` and
`AsyncDataset.map_batches` are
unexported, undocumented, and uncalled — the sharded variant warned at
runtime
to use `build_cache` instead — and dropping them makes their whole
support chain
dead, including the `_DatasetTransform` hierarchy in `_preprocessor.py`.
Tests
that existed only to exercise the removed code are deleted with it.

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
[grug] Resume MoE checkpoints across FSDP and pipeline training (#8974)

Save pipeline MoE checkpoints as one unsplit model and optimizer tree
using ordinary Levanter checkpoint APIs. FSDP and PP can load the same
state with different device meshes, pipeline schedules, and layer
splits. The completed step and pending router updates survive the
transition. The step limit counts total updates across restarts; an
explicit checkpoint root and save cadence control persistence.

Grug maps stage-local state to global layer paths at the checkpoint
boundary. Levanter adapts JaxPP device buffers and reconstructs the
destination MPMD placement without gathering model or optimizer tensors.
Shared optimizer counters are read on each destination stage. Standard
completion metadata and discovery replace the separate latest pointer
and source-topology checks. The model and optimizer structures must
agree; checkpoints written by the pipeline trainer also record model
configuration, optimizer settings, and precision for validation.
Changing token grouping can change MoE routing and subsequent optimizer
updates.

Fixes #8972
